newsitem.title: IRAQ: Kurdish militia reports fresh clashes near Iran.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish militia reports fresh clashes near Iran.

text.p: Rival Iraqi Kurdish forces clashed at five villages near the Iranian border, and again outside the main northern city of Arbil, officials from one of the factions said on Friday.

Shorsh Jalalal of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) told Reuters that rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) forces struck at PUK positions in the villages around Halabja, 10 km (six miles) from the Iranian border.
"But with the support of new forces moved into position, control of three of the villages was regained late last night," Jalalal said.
He said the villages of Kedeferi, Girdanaze and Girdago were back in PUK hands but did not name the other two, still under KDP control.

The attacks marked an expansion of the front in the latest inter-Kurdish fighting, which took on fresh urgency last weekend when Iraqi government forces intervened on behalf of the KDP to expel the PUK from Arbil, capital of northern Iraq.
Baghdad's move into the Western-protected north drew U.S. cruise missile attacks on targets south of the Iraqi capital. Washington said on Thursday that Iraqi government troops had later withdrawn.
However, opposition groups report continued Iraqi involvement in support of a KDP advance along the main road toward the PUK stronghold of Sulaimaniya.
A Reuters reporter who toured the region south of Arbil on Thursday saw Iraqi tanks dug in but no evidence that they were engaged in the latest fighting.
